vakbeschrijving.nl:
This course bridges the theoretical Earth System knowledge acquired in the previous Principles of Earth System courses with practical applications in subsurface engineering. It explores how Earth science principles underpin engineering activities in various parts of the subsurface, including: 1) the upper 50 meters of the subsurface relevant to geotechnical engineering, 2) the deeper subsurface, used for water and heat extraction, energy storage, and waste disposal, and 3) critical raw material extraction at any depth. The course emhasises the Earth Science aspects of these engineering applications, focusing on a) methods for characterising subsurface properties, b) the nature and implications of geoscientific uncertainties, and c) the relative importance of geoscientific aspects in the engineering application at stake. There is attention for, but less emphasis upon, the engineering aspects of the applications and the dynamic behavior related to the engineering, which are part of other courses of the BSc and, particularly, the more specialized tracks in the EC&T MSc. At this stage, the students will learn about how Earth System theory and practice is needed for engineering in the subsurface.  

The course is organised into three main components:  

  1. Predictability of the subsurface characteristics and the related uncertainty 

This part builds directly on the preceding Earth Subsurface course, which introduced the character and variability of the subsurface.  . This will be continued here focusing on the predictability of these heterogeneities and their related uncertainty.  

2. Characterisation of Earth subsurface properties 

This component addresses methods for investigating and quantifying subsurface properties. Topics include geophysical and petrophysical methodologies, cores and cuttings as direct subsurface sediment and rock samples, and shallow subsurface methodologies such as Cone Penetration Tests. Last, upscaling of properties in geomodelling will be discussed. 

3. Impact of Earth subsurface character on engineering applications 

Here, students integrate knowledge from the first two components to explore how subsurface characteristics influence subsurface engineering applications . This relates to the dynamic response, uncertainty propagation, project efficiency, and project safety. 

Given the broad scope of the subject, the course cannot cover all topics in equal depth. Instead, selected topics and applications are explored in detail to help students understand the complete workflow from data acquisition to engineering interpretation. Other topics are introduced through overview lectures to provide broader context. The selected case studies are aligned with examples from other BSc courses, ensuring that students gain both a comprehensive overview of the field and a foundation for specialisation in the MSc tracks. 

Lecture topics are complemented by hands-on practical exercises and project work to allow students to get to know the data, materials, and techniques actively. Alignment with the Data Learning Line is made to work on similar data and data analysis techniques. 

The course concludes with a summative written examination.

leerdoelen.nl:
1. Identify how Principles of Earth System theoretical knowledge is used in shallow to deep subsurface engineering

  2. Explain the origin and nature of the character and scales of heterogeneities of Earth Subsurface properties and state

  3. Apply some direct and indirect characterisation methodologies of subsurface properties and states 

  4. Infer how subsurface character and states, and their heterogeneity and predictability impact engineering, its projections and uncertainty

toetsing.nl:
Students are required to submit reports for six different practical exercises, which will be assessed for formative feedback.

100% Exam (3h), closed-book, formula sheet provided (week 4.3, resit week 4.10)

cr_expected_prior_knowledge_nld.nl: To participate in the course, active participation is needed in ECTB2110 Earth Subsurface course and a pass grade is needed for the Year 1 ECTB1120A Principles of Earth System course. Courses in the ‘Geodata Fundamentals’ learning line are expected prior knowledge particularly for the geophysics data analysis.
